samples.summary: `levelOf()` silently repairs out-of-band levels, which the task's own Out-of-scope list and the new design-doc paragraph say the gesture does not do
samples.evidence: `levelOf` clamps to `[0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL]` and the plan writes `levelOf(block) + delta`, so an item stored at level 48 is rewritten to 7 on outdent (asserted in test/model/list-level.test.ts:146). docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md:57 lists "Auto-normalizing levels that are already broken" as out of scope, and docs/design/docs/docs.md:171 states "Levels that are *already* inconsistent … are read as-is rather than normalized". Defensible for NaN/Infinity, but the doc and the stated scope should say what the code actually does (repair on write) rather than the opposite.

samples.summary: Design doc says "All six writers route through it" but then enumerates seven handlers
samples.evidence: handleTab, handleIndent, handleOutdent (text-editor.ts) + indent/outdent in editor.ts + indent/outdent in text-box-editor.ts = 7 call sites, all of which the diff does route through planListLevelChanges.

samples.summary: The new undo/batching contract (each gesture is now one `doc.batch()` unit, `snapshot()` moved inside) is a behavioral decision recorded only in code comments, not in the design doc that this change otherwise updates
samples.evidence: editor.ts / text-box-editor.ts / text-editor.ts all wrap indent/outdent/Tab in `doc.batch()` with long justifying comments about undo granularity and Yorkie change count, but the new docs.md section (lines 136-173) never mentions that a list-level gesture is now a single undo unit — a user-visible semantics change from the previous per-block writes.
searchedFor: docs/design/docs/docs.md §Changing a list level carries the subtree

samples.summary: The walker fixes (context-blocks and doc.blockParentMap) change behavior for every other consumer of `forEachBlockInSelection`, which is unrequested scope not recorded anywhere
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts's multi-block branch now reads `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` instead of `this.doc.document.blocks`, and editor.ts:1729 switches the cursor-only fallback from `layout.blockParentMap` to `doc.blockParentMap`. Both walkers are shared by other formatting commands (style/alignment/list-toggle paths), so this silently alters header/footer behavior beyond the list-level gesture. It looks like a genuine fix, but neither the todo (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md:48) nor docs.md mentions the header/footer correction as part of the change.

samples.summary: `applyListLevelChanges` and `siblingsOf` are copy-pasted across three editors rather than shared alongside the new pure planner
samples.evidence: Near-identical `applyListLevelChanges` bodies exist in editor.ts (~1600), text-box-editor.ts (~819) and text-editor.ts (~2720), and `siblingsOf` is duplicated in editor.ts and text-editor.ts. The planner itself was correctly extracted to model/list-level.ts; the thin apply/sibling helpers are the remaining divergence risk (only editor.ts's copy does markDirty).
